title: FloodGuard Private Flood Policy — General Rating Rules
content:
General rating rules of the FloodGuard Private Flood Policy, with the zone building rates. Several clauses of these rules have been retired and are shown below as no longer in force; the remaining clause and the zone rate table continue to apply.

## Zone building rates

| Flood zone | Zone building rate (per 1,000 USD of rated building amount) |
|---|---|
| X | 0.64 |
| A | 3.87 |
| AE | 2.96 |
| VE | 6.42 |

## Clause in force — contents premium

The contents premium is the contents limit divided by 1,000 and multiplied by the tier's contents rate per 1,000.

*Hypothetical example.* A contents limit of 60,000 USD on a tier whose contents rate per 1,000 is 1.31 gives a contents premium of 60 multiplied by 1.31, which is 78.60 USD.

## Retired clauses — no longer in force

The following clauses are **no longer in force**. Each has been superseded by the current basis and is not applied to any premium:

1. *Building premium.* The former clause that rated the building premium as the building limit divided by 1,000, multiplied by the zone building rate of the flood zone and by the tier's building rate factor, raised by the tier's zone VE surcharge percentage in zone VE and reduced by the tier's elevation credit percentage when the elevation certificate shows the lowest floor at least one foot above base flood elevation — no longer in force.
2. *Annual premium.* The former clause that made the annual premium the building plus contents premium, reduced by the tier's companion discount percentage where the companion discount applies, rounded half-up to the cent and never less than the tier's minimum annual premium, with the policy fee charged on top each term and never discounted — no longer in force.
3. *Midterm changes.* The former clause under which a limit or zone change never re-rates the term midterm except through a limit increase, whose annual premium change is the difference between the annual premium with and without the increase, prorated from the date it attaches to the expiration date over the calendar days in the term, rounded half-up to the cent, with nothing billed below the tier's minimum premium change — no longer in force.
4. *Renewal rating basis.* The former clause that rated the indicated renewal premium on the zone, elevation and limits on file on the renewal offer date — no longer in force.
5. *Renewal rate cap.* The former clause that made the renewal term premium the smaller of that indicated premium and the expiring term premium increased by the tier's renewal rate cap percentage, rounded half-up to the cent — no longer in force.

The zone building rates in the table above remain valid figures of the FloodGuard Private Flood Policy; only the retired handling clauses have been withdrawn.

superseded_clauses: The building premium is building_limit divided by 1,000, multiplied by the zone_building_rate of the flood zone and by building_rate_factor, raised by zones_rated_extra_pct in zone VE and reduced by elevation_credit_pct when the elevation certificate shows the lowest floor at least one foot above base flood elevation.

The annual premium is the building plus contents premium, reduced by companion_discount_pct where flood_agg_companion_discount applies, rounded half-up to the cent and never less than minimum_annual_premium; the policy fee is charged on top of it each term and is never discounted.
At renewal the indicated premium is rated on the zone, elevation and limits on file on the renewal offer date
the renewal term premium is the smaller of that indicated premium and the expiring term_premium increased by renewal_rate_cap_pct, rounded half-up to the cent.

A limit or zone change never re-rates the term midterm except through a limit increase, whose annual premium change is the difference between the annual premium with and without the increase and is prorated from the date it attaches to the expiration date over the calendar days in the term, rounded half-up to the cent; below min_premium_change nothing is billed.
